finding: Before the routing fix, a standby rejection after any successful command published tracking_fault=true, setting a planner stop that standby cannot release.

sources.meaning: Current reject retains local stop and gates tracking_fault by reference.active; historical condition lacked that gate.
trackingFaultCallback: false releases only with recovery candidate and EXEC_TRAJ; true sets tracking stop even without target.
No-active-target safety callback republishes zero while tracking_safety_stop_active remains set.

inference_limits: The /tracking_fault topic was not recorded. First fault times below are inferred from the historical reject condition and the first rejection after any delivery. Speed-limit and command values are direct successful-status observations.
fix_scope: Gate tracking_fault=true by active navigation reference; preserve immediate local base stop, arm watchdog and all later collision/freshness/deadline/speed-limit checks. Existing planner latch is not force-cleared.
interpretation: Historical small base displacement cannot be used as evidence that arm optimization reduces base interference or improves avoidance efficiency.
